newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share market disappoints with Monday "blues".
newsitem.headline: NZ share market disappoints with Monday "blues".

text.p: * NZ shares end lower despite Friday strength in U.S., U.K.
* Volume boosted by lines in Air NZ and CIL
New Zealand's share market turned on a lacklustre performance on Monday in stark contrast to the strong markets in the U.S. and U.K. on Friday.

"It's a real case of the Monday blues. New Zealand is suffering from a lack of interest," said Don Turkington of Cavill White Securities. "It's a very, very soggy market and disappointing in view of strong overseas market in the U.S. and U.K.," he said.
The indicator NZSE-40 capital index fell 12.96 points. Volume of $40 million was boosted by large lines in Corporate Investments and Air New Zealand.
Brokers said the New Zealand market was possibly suffering as a result of the political impasse since the October 12 election.
The 4.0 million Air NZ "B" shares reported at $3.55 each were the two percent of the rights issue which were not taken up, and have been placed with institutions. The "B" shares closed at $3.60.

Market leader Telecom fell eight cents to $7.41 on light volume while the Fletcher stocks were a mixed bag. Energy continues to star, rising four cents to $4.27 but Paper shed another five cents to an all-time low of $2.47.
Corporate Investments was steady on 63 cents on volume of 4.3 million.
